§11.1.2 Labels

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-labels · charts labels

✅ Normative

The category labels and series names of a chart table MUST be text printed on the chart — an axis tick, a legend entry, a direct label — copied verbatim. A label MUST NOT carry unit text imported from elsewhere on the page, colour words, chart-type words or an expanded abbreviation, and two dimensions MUST NOT be merged into one label.

Each value in a chart table is located by the labels on its row and in its column, so the labels are the lookup key of the whole table: a value under the wrong label is a wrong value.

Which label goes where

Chart Row label Column label
Single series the category (Cleaners) — see Values and Tolerances§11.1.4 the series name, or the value-axis title when no name is printed
Two-dimensional (grouped, stacked, multi-line) the category (China) the series (Ride hailing)
Grouped or nested categories the category, with its printed group (axis tier) in a column of its own where the category alone repeats the series

A value MUST sit at the intersection of exactly the labels that locate it: its category's row and its series' column. Dimensions stay independent — 2024 in the row and Revenue in the column, never one label 2024 - Revenue.

Verbatim, and what "no units" means

Each label is one printed string, copied whole — SEA, > 15000, Option-Adjusted Spread (OAS), REDBIKE (Akira), first-day-of-month price. Parentheses printed inside a legend entry are part of the legend text and MUST be kept.

The no-units requirement forbids importing unit text from elsewhere on the page into a label. Where the axis corner prints (millions of euros) and the tick prints 2024, the label is 2024, not 2024 (millions of euros). Likewise Revenue, not Revenue (USD bn), when the unit prints as an axis note rather than inside the legend entry. The unit note itself is not dropped: it stays in the output as the chart's own text (see Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1).

A label MUST NOT be rewritten:

  • no colour words — Blue line - GDP Growth is GDP Growth;
  • no descriptive or chart-type suffixes — no (line), no (bars);
  • no expanded abbreviations — SEA stays SEA.

Positions the axis does not label

A position on a printed, regularly labeled axis that carries no tick label of its own is labeled by its axis value — 2023 on a year axis ticked every third year, 2500 on a bin axis labeled every other bin. That label is a reading against printed calibration, not invented text (see Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1).

Several charts with the same labels

Each chart or panel has its own chart table with its own printed title in <caption> (see Multiple Charts and Reference Ink§11.1.3), so charts that reuse one label set are told apart by their captions, without altering their labels. The caption appears once inside the table, first or last according to reading order (see Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3).

  • The twin pies in Legend and Overlay Values§11.2.4 reuse every slice name; each pie's title (Month of September 2025: $346B, Fiscal Year 2025 to Date: $7,010B) is what distinguishes them.
  • The solar panels in Multiple Charts and Reference Ink§11.1.3 need nothing more: China with 619 appears only in the avoided-emissions panel.

A point that no printed label can locate is not rendered in the chart table (see Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1); the unnamed companion curve in Legend and Overlay Values§11.2.4 is the standing example.

✅ Sample — mobility-survey-2024_p13

Four legend series over eight labeled regions, every value printed on its bar: 32 values, rows labeled from the axis and columns from the legend, verbatim. Region abbreviations stay as printed (SEA, ME, NEA). The values printed in heavier type are bold in the table; the red ones carry no colour mark, since colour on a data label is styling.
